correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the proof. A finite graph has covering dimension one; its product with the zero-dimensional compact metrizable Cantor set has dimension at most one, and the closed horizontal interval in a fiber gives the lower bound. Projection onto the totally disconnected factor shows that the fibers are exactly the connected components. For any two fibers and any uniform error δ<1/2, the map (t,s) ↦ (Re(b(s)−a(t)), Im(a(t)−b(s))) is a continuous self-map of [-1,1]^2: both real coordinates are bounded by 2δ. Its fixed-point equation is t−is=b(s)−a(t), so the actual horizontal and vertical images intersect even across different fibers. Pairwise intersection of connected fiber images rules out a separation of the entire range. Pointwise inversion gives spectrum equal to range, and the Cantor-coordinate function realizes continuum many singleton spectral components. Thus all finite classes are nonempty and none with n≥2 is dense. The quoted zero-dimensional guarantee is for infinite compact spaces. No computation or numerical certificate is needed.
residual_risks: The claimed radius is sufficient; no optimality or characterization of all one-dimensional spaces is proved.
